system.summary: The source study's own reading of this plate already names the phenomenon: monocytes, which carry TLR4, respond to LPS first, while B, T and NK cells - which have little or no LPS receptor - respond only at later time points, attributed by the authors to inter-cellular communication through IL-6 or other monocyte-released factors. The literature fixes a receptor asymmetry a base model can use: TLR4 and the GM-CSF, G-CSF and IL-3 receptors are restricted to myelomonocytic cells among PBMC, so LPS and the three colony-stimulating factors have no direct receptor on the staged lymphocyte gates, whereas IFNAR2 is on essentially all monocytes, B cells and CD4/CD8 T cells, and the IFN-gamma transducing chain IFNGR2 is high on myeloid, moderate on B and poor on T cells - the exact rank order of the direct IFN-gamma responses here. Two secreted candidates have human support: LPS induces IFN-beta transcription and secretion with STAT1 phosphorylation and ISGs in primary human PBMC (and an IFNAR2-blocking antibody abolishes the late type I IFN-dependent arm in human myeloid cells), and LPS, GM-CSF and IL-3 all induce IL-6 gene expression in purified human monocytes, with IL-6R on most CD4 T cells but only a small, variable fraction of CD8 T and B cells - the population signature the late STAT3 rise follows. The main tension is timing: bulk monocyte IL-6/TNF protein release (mRNA 2-4 h, protein 4-6 h) and autocrine type I IFN loops (ISGF3 far stronger at 4 h than 1 h) are slower than the 60-120 min onset seen here. Known STAT kinetics (nuclear pY-STAT1 maximal at 20-30 min, cleared within ~60 min once receptor input stops) set the deactivation half of every cycle.
system.scope: Human peripheral blood leukocytes: primary CD14+ monocytes, monocyte-derived macrophages and dendritic cells, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, B cells, NK cells, whole blood and PBMC, ex vivo at 37 C, stimulated with LPS, IFN-alpha/beta, IFN-gamma, IL-6, GM-CSF, G-CSF or IL-3, minutes to 48 h. Mechanistic JAK/STAT models and several LPS-to-IFN-beta loop experiments come from mouse macrophages, mouse dendritic cells or human hepatoma/erythroid cells and are marked as such.
unknowns: The identity of the factor(s) reaching the lymphocytes is not measured here; two factors with the same STAT signature and receptor distribution are indistinguishable in these data.

Whether human monocytes secrete enough type I interferon protein within 60-120 min at 30 ng/ml LPS to phosphorylate lymphocyte STATs: published autocrine-loop and cytokine-release kinetics are slower.
Whether human T cells express a functional G-CSF receptor is disputed (Boneberg 2000: absent from lymphocytes; Franzke 2003: present in class I- and II-restricted T cells).
Whether G-CSF induces IL-6 in human monocytes is untested in the study showing IL-3 and GM-CSF do; G-CSF is reported to suppress rather than augment monokine release.
IL-6R and gp130 on human NK cells are essentially undocumented; the subset studies report CD4 T, CD8 T, B cells and monocytes but not NK cells.
Whether the unstimulated wells' slow rise is basal secretion: plating/adherence induces monokine mRNA within 30-90 min but secretion required a second signal (Haskill 1988).
Whether a secreted factor is well mixed in a 200 ul well: diffusion competing with receptor consumption produces niches of 80-120 um in dense cell populations.
No measurement was found of type I IFN or IL-6 protein in the medium of an LPS-stimulated human PBMC well at 1, 2 and 4 h at 30 ng/ml - the quantity that would settle the question.

facts.statement: Human monocytes carry about 3,000-7,000 IFN-gamma binding sites per cell (Ka 4-12 x 10^8 M^-1) and degrade about 5,000 IFN-gamma molecules per cell per hour at 37 C, giving both a receptor number and a ligand-consumption rate for a shared 200 ul medium.

evidence.title: Demonstration and partial characterization of the interferon-gamma receptor on human mononuclear phagocytes
evidence.supports: Quantifies receptor number, affinity, internalisation and ligand degradation rate on primary human monocytes.
evidence.quote: Monocytes degraded 125I-IFN gamma into trichloroacetic acid-soluble counts at 37 degrees C but not at 4 degrees C, at an approximate rate of 5,000 molecules/cell per h.
evidence.context_note: Primary human blood monocytes at 37 C.

facts.statement: A relay through a sensing population is documented in human PBMC: monocytes, NK cells and T cells do not respond to CpG alone but are activated when plasmacytoid dendritic cells are present in the same culture.

evidence.title: Quantitative expression of toll-like receptor 1-10 mRNA in cellular subsets of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells and sensitivity to CpG oligodeoxynucleotides
evidence.supports: Demonstrates in human PBMC that non-sensing populations respond to a TLR ligand only in the presence of the sensing population - the same well-level relay logic as the intent's question.
evidence.quote: Despite low expression of TLR9, monocytes, NK cells, and T cells did not respond to CpG ODN in the absence of PDC but were activated in the presence of PDC.
evidence.context_note: Purified human PBMC subsets and co-cultures; the ligand is CpG, not LPS, and dendritic cells are not staged in the intent's gating.

facts.statement: Paracrine type I interferon from a small fraction of early responders coordinates the antiviral response of the whole population in mouse dendritic cells - a precedent for a fast, interferon-mediated relay within one culture.

evidence.title: Single-cell RNA-seq reveals dynamic paracrine control of cellular variation
evidence.locator: Abstract; microfluidic isolation and secretion-blocking experiments
evidence.supports: Blocking secretion and extracellular signalling showed the population response is coordinated by interferon-mediated paracrine signalling from early-responding cells.
evidence.quote: we show that this response is coordinated by interferon-mediated paracrine signalling from these precocious cells
evidence.context_note: Mouse bone-marrow-derived dendritic cells with LPS; the intent's system is human PBMC and the readout is STAT phosphorylation, not transcription.

facts.statement: A secreted factor in a 200 ul well is not automatically uniform: diffusion competing with consumption by receptor-bearing cells generates niches of 80-120 um whose size scales with the density of consuming cells.

evidence.title: A Tunable Diffusion-Consumption Mechanism of Cytokine Propagation Enables Plasticity in Cell-to-Cell Communication in the Immune System
evidence.supports: Quantifies the length scale of cytokine communication and shows consumption produces sharp spatial boundaries and cell-to-cell variance in exposure.
evidence.context_note: Mouse tissue and in vitro systems; the intent's well is a suspension, so this bounds rather than refutes the well-mixed assumption.

facts.statement: Arcsinh with cofactor 5 is the standard transformation for mass cytometry ion counts, mapping channels to a comparable range; it is near-linear close to zero, which is where the B- and NK-cell pSTAT1 baselines sit.

evidence.title: CyTOF workflow: differential discovery in high-throughput high-dimensional cytometry datasets
evidence.supports: States the standard arcsinh cofactor-5 transformation for CyTOF marker intensities and its purpose.
evidence.quote: It is common practice to transform CyTOF marker intensities using, for example, arcsinh (inverse hyperbolic sine) with cofactor 5 to make the distributions more symmetric and to map them to a comparable range of expression, which is important for clustering.
evidence.context_note: Methodological workflow built on the same Bodenmiller PBMC data family.

facts.statement: Mass-tag cellular barcoding pools all 96 wells into one sample stained and acquired together, which is why any well-to-well difference must have arisen in the well before fixation; the same study reports PBMC signalling dynamics and cell-to-cell communication as its subject.

evidence.title: Multiplexed mass cytometry profiling of cellular states perturbed by small-molecule regulators
evidence.supports: The source study of these data: seven metal tags multiplex a whole 96-well plate, applied to human PBMC signalling dynamics and cell-to-cell communication.
evidence.quote: We used seven tags to multiplex an entire 96-well plate, and applied MCB to characterize human peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) signaling dynamics and cell-to-cell communication, signaling variability between PBMCs from eight human donors, and the effects of 27 inhibitors on this system.
evidence.context_note: The experiment being re-analysed (Cytobank 15711).

facts.statement: The authors of the source study read the same plate as inter-cellular communication: monocytes, which express TLR4, responded to LPS first, while B, T and NK cells - with little or no LPS receptor - responded only at later time points, attributed to IL-6 or other monocyte-released factors.

evidence.title: Multiplexed mass cytometry profiling of cellular states perturbed by small-molecule regulators
evidence.locator: Results, PBMC time course (SPADE analysis of the LPS response)
evidence.supports: Reports that monocytes respond first to LPS with p38, ERK and NF-kB peaking at 15-30 min, that B, T and NK cells respond only later (T and NK STAT3/STAT5 after 2 h, B-cell STAT1 after 4 h), and attributes this to inter-cellular communication through IL-6 or other monocyte-released factors such as TNF-alpha.
evidence.context_note: The very experiment being re-analysed; I could not retrieve the full text through an open route, so this item carries no quote.

facts.statement: A modern single-cell study of human PBMC stimulated with LPS reported that only monocytes were transcriptionally activated, with no distinct interferon-stimulated-gene response in T, B or NK cells - evidence against a strong bystander effect, though at 10 ng/ml, 24 h and on mRNA rather than STAT phosphorylation.

evidence.title: Single Cell Analysis of Blood Mononuclear Cells Stimulated Through Either LPS or Anti-CD3 and Anti-CD28
evidence.supports: In CITE-seq of human PBMC stimulated with LPS at 10 ng/ml for 24 h, activation was confined to monocytes, with ISG-high states reported for NK cells only after anti-CD3/CD28.
evidence.context_note: Human PBMC with LPS, but a single 24 h endpoint and a transcriptome readout, which can miss a transient 2-4 h STAT response.

facts.statement: Handling and plating alone induce monokine mRNA in human monocytes within 30-90 min, but secretion of those mediators required a second, LPS-derived signal - which bears directly on whether the unstimulated wells' drift is basal secretion or an unrelated process.

evidence.title: Adherence induces selective mRNA expression of monocyte mediators and proto-oncogenes
evidence.supports: Adherence rapidly induces TNF, IL-1beta and CSF-1 mRNA in human monocytes but is not sufficient for secretion.
evidence.quote: Although all of these genes could be induced by adherence, actual secretion of the mediators required the exposure to a second signal derived from LPS.
evidence.context_note: Primary human monocytes adhering to plastic; the intent's cells are a rested non-adherent suspension in a deep-well block.

facts.statement: Quantitative proteomes of 28 primary human immune cell populations in resting and activated states, including secreted proteins, provide per-population copy numbers for receptors and ligands where a model needs initial values (immprot.org).

evidence.title: Social network architecture of human immune cells unveiled by quantitative proteomics
evidence.supports: Reports protein copy numbers across 28 primary human hematopoietic populations in steady and activated states, integrating total and secreted proteomes to map intercellular communication.
evidence.context_note: Primary human immune cell populations; I did not retrieve the individual copy numbers for the receptors and STATs of this model.

notes: Correction from the previous attempt: the three sources I had cited by bare PubMed number (11739558 Bernabei 2001 IFN-gammaR2; 8123762 the 1993 monocyte cytokine-gene study; 1353064 Zola 1992 IL-6R on blood lymphocytes) are now cited by their PubMed URL in both `source` and `url`; no item cites a bare number, and no content was otherwise changed for those items. Coverage gaps. (1) The source paper's own LPS-relay passage is reported from its Results but carries no quote: nature.com, PMC and the Europe PMC full-text XML were all inaccessible to my fetcher and the one open PDF returned undecoded binary, so only the abstract text is quotable for 10.1038/nbt.2317. (2) No source was found measuring type I IFN or IL-6 protein in the medium of an LPS-stimulated human PBMC well at 1, 2 and 4 h at 30 ng/ml - the decisive quantity. The cytokine kinetics I did find (mRNA 2-4 h, protein 4-6 h; ISGF3 far stronger at 4 h than 1 h) are slower than the 60-120 min onset in these data and are returned with stance contradicts rather than omitted. (3) NK cells are the least documented population: I found no quantification of IFNGR2, IL-6R or gp130 on human NK cells, so the NK entries rest on curated pathway records rather than population-specific experiments - which matters, because the NK gate carries two of the observations the question turns on. (4) G-CSF is the weakest arm of hypothesis 2: no source tests whether G-CSF induces IL-6 in human monocytes, and the one source on G-CSF and monokines reports suppression, returned as contradicting. (5) Whether human T cells carry a functional G-CSF receptor is a live conflict between Boneberg 2000 and Franzke 2003; both are returned with opposite stances. (6) Lawlor 2021 (human PBMC, LPS, 24 h, CITE-seq) reports monocyte-restricted activation and is returned as contradicting a strong bystander effect, with the caveat that a single 24 h transcriptome endpoint can miss a transient 2-4 h STAT response. (7) Haskill 1988 argues against the basal-secretion reading of the Reference drift and is returned with stance contradicts. (8) Quotes: verbatim text is included only where I could read it in a retrieved document (mostly abstracts and a few Results sentences); entries whose source I could reach only through metadata carry `supports` without a quote. (9) I could not verify IL-27 p28/EBI3 release kinetics in LPS-stimulated human monocytes from a citable primary source, so the IL-27 expansion reaction carries only the curated Reactome reaction and no timing fact. (10) Identifiers: receptor species are lumped receptor-plus-JAK complexes per decision 11 and deliberately carry no UniProt id (a complex is not one protein); only a GO compartment is given. The three STAT5 species use the STAT5A accession, since the panel's clone 47 does not distinguish STAT5A from STAT5B. (11) Reaction count: the per-population enumeration is deliberate - the discrimination in this question lives in which population responds to which factor, so the same conversion appears once per population rather than as one generic entry.
